text:
Sophia Park: Heads up — nightly eval shows a sharp quality drop on the 'support_faq_v2' prompt set starting last night. Top-line: qa_f1 down ~9% vs baseline.

Matt G: saw that. Any clue if model weight or infra changed? :thinking:

eval-bot: nightly-evals/2024-11-15 02:34 UTC — job=nightly-evals, model=rw-v1-quant, variant=8-bit, eval_set=support_faq_v2, metric=qa_f1, baseline=0.78, current=0.71, alert=regression

Rachel H: we had a runtime change yesterday that altered default sampling params for dedicated endpoints — top_p went from 0.95 -> 1.0 to match streaming behavior. That could increase diversity and break evals.

Lee: also worth noting quantization + nondet seeds can amplify variance. Are eval runs fixing seed? I think nightly runs didn't pass --seed explicitly.

Sophia Park: good catch. CI job shows no --seed flag. Can someone try a quick repro with fixed seed + top_p 0.95 vs 1.0 on the quantized binary?

Matt G: running a quick local reproduce now. Command I used:
```
./rw-infer --model rw-v1-quant --prompt-file tests/support_faq_v2.json --top_p 1.0 --temperature 0.0 --seed 42 --batch 1 --num-samples 1
```

Matt G: with top_p=1.0 seed=42 got answer A (incorrect in eval). With top_p=0.95 seed=42 got answer B (matches baseline). So looks like sampling param change is the culprit, not model weights.

Rachel H: confirms: quantized kernel has slightly different numerical tie-breakers but shouldn't change deterministic path if seed fixed. So two fixes: revert default top_p in runtime, and make nightly evals pass an explicit --seed.

Sophia Park: agree. @Matt can you open a rollback PR for the default top_p? @Rachel can you add --seed=12345 to nightly job and re-run overnight? Also add a short note to eval dashboard explaining nondeterminism risk for quantized runs.

ci-bot: created issue #4521 — "nightly evals: pass deterministic seed; document sampling sensitivity" assigned to Rachel H, due 2024-11-18

Matt G: PR opened: runtime#987 revert default top_p to 0.95. Will coordinate canary.

Lee: propose adding an explicit eval permutation: for each prompt set run 3 seeds (42, 123, 999) and report median to avoid sporadic flakiness.

Sophia Park: good idea. Let's do median across 3 seeds but keep single-seed smoke to catch big regressions faster. I'll update the eval playbook.

Rachel H: scheduled canary with quantized model + top_p=0.95 + seeds [42,123,999] on canary infra; will post results in morning.

Sophia Park: thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
